newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn delays ruling on D.Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Bonn delays ruling on D.Telekom.

text.p: The German government said on Monday it would delay taking any regulatory action against phone giant Deutsche Telekom until an appeal by the company is decided in the next few weeks in administrative court.

The Post and Telecommunications Ministry told Telekom on July 1 it had until midnight on July 14 to allow its rivals to gain access to its local telephone networks, a so-called agreement on unbundled interconnection.
This would allow rivals to connect directly to the telephone access lines of residential and business customers without being forced to pay for switching services from Deutsche Telekom.
This is a crucial cost issue for new companies getting ready to compete against Telekom when Germany's telecommunications market is deregulated next year.
Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch issued the ultimatum to Telekom in a regulatory ruling, but Telekom has appealed against the ruling in administrative court.
If the court backs the government Telekom would have to either make a new offer to rivals or face penalty proceedings that could lead to fines of up to one million marks.

Klaus-Dieter Scheuerle, the designated president of the new telecoms watchdog Regulatory Agency, criticised the company for not fulfilling its legal responsibilities under Germany's Telecommunications Act.

"It is inappropriate and does not reflect the facts when Telekom chief Ron Sommer claims that actions are taking place equivalent to appropriation," Scheuerle told the daily Die Welt newspaper in an interview to appear on Tuesday.
Scheuerle, the chief of the ministry's regulatory department, said he did not believe that Telekom was prepared to reach any agreement on interconnection with its competitors.
"I presume that Telekom at least in the beginning will take every decision to court with which it does not agree," he said.
The original ruling was based on a complaint by three companies, including the Mannesmann Arcor group and O.Tel.O, the joint venture of utilities RWE and Veba AG, Telekom's chief domestic rivals.
Ulf Bohla, chairman of O.Tel.O, said it was necessary for the government to carry out its rulings quickly and criticised the government's delay.
"It is the wrong signal when the regulator, that is the ministry, caves in at the first sign of resistance," he said in a statement.
"The Telecommunications Act gives the regulatory authority a strong position. This decision shows that it is not using it," he added.
